target_paper.title: In-Context Molecular Property Prediction with LLMs: A Blinding Study on Memorization and Knowledge Conflicts

generation.parameters: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 4000 (ICL) / 800 (zero-shot), 2 runs per configuration as in the paper; OpenAI endpoint instead of the Azure deployment
generation.battery: zero-shot 1,128 x 5 + analyses 12 + predictions 600 = 6,252 calls; molecule split and fold order reproduced exactly (MersenneTwister port, 150/150 test names)

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN §1; human double-coding pending
results.note: Zero-shot r 0.406 vs 0.407; 1000-shot r 76.6 [69.2, 82.8] vs 75.6 [68.5, 81.5]; 60-shot r 37.6 [21.7, 52.2] vs 42.9 [28.2, 56.1] (overlapping, larger run-to-run spread at temperature 0.7); memorization indicators unchanged (3-significant-digit exact matches 0.21% vs 0.14%, retention 10.0% vs 9.7% at the ~10% coincidence floor). The claim that many-shot in-context examples lift the correlation without verbatim recall reproduces.

reproducibility_frictions_observed: pipeline is Julia; Julia not installed, so prompts, parsing and the Mersenne-Twister molecule split were ported to Python and validated against the archived chats (2,700/2,700 replies re-parse; 150/150 test names)
original runs went through an Azure deployment; the OpenAI endpoint served gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 (9 fingerprints)
one 1000-shot call is ~30k tokens; prompt caching makes cost depend on call ordering
